summary: This bill directs the Secretary of Energy to reestablish the National Coal Council under its November 2021 charter to advise on coal matters and exempts the council from the federal advisory committee termination requirement.

scores.thoughts: The bill reestablishes an advisory council within the Department of Energy. This entails minor administrative and operational costs for staffing and meetings, representing a small expansion of government activity and spending. No funding authorizations or cuts are specified, so the effect is tangential and minimal.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, credits, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill addresses only the reestablishment of a coal industry advisory council and has no connection to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions in the bill relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The legislation does not address immigration, border policy, visas, or related protections.
No content in the bill pertains to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill is confined to domestic energy advisory functions and does not affect military or defense budgets or policy.

The bill reestablishes a federal advisory council specifically tasked with providing recommendations on coal and the coal industry. Coal is a major fossil fuel, and institutionalizing industry input tends to favor continued coal use over stricter environmental or climate regulations. This constitutes a moderate, clear pro-coal tilt with implications for environmental policy.
No provisions relate to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety-net policies.
The bill has no bearing on schools, education funding, or school choice.
No references to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances appear in the text.
The legislation does not address policing, sentencing, or criminal justice reform.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization measures are included.
Any spending impact is negligible and indirect; the bill does not engage with deficit reduction or debt policy.
The bill contains nothing related to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
No foreign aid, international assistance, or diplomatic funding provisions are present.
The bill does not address voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight content exists.
While the council addresses coal industry matters that could indirectly touch employment, the bill itself makes no direct changes to labor law, union rights, or worker protections.
The legislation does not engage with religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
